info.title: Audit service
info.description:
The Audit service records who did what, to which resource and when, for ADSP applications.

**Read this before integrating.**
- A `202` from `POST /audit/v1/{namespace}/events` does **not** mean every event was stored. Inspect `accepted`, `duplicates` and `rejected` in the body. Rejected events are not stored and are not resent.
- `403` means a missing role **or** a namespace that is not the caller's. `404` on the actions endpoint means no catalog is registered for the namespace. `503` means retry.
- Roles: `audit-writer` writes events, `audit-reader` reads events and action catalogs, `audit-admin` manages failed events.
- Retention periods are applied when an event is written. Changing retention configuration affects only events written afterward.

Use **Authorize** with a bearer token to try requests from this page. Writing to a namespace you do not own returns `403`.

get.summary: List all action catalogs visible to the caller.
get.description:
Requires the `audit-reader` role, held in the tenant or as a Core role. Returns every catalog registered in
audit-service:actions-<application> for the caller's tenant and for Core (such as the platform services), so a
client can discover the available namespaces and actions. As for the single-namespace endpoint, each catalog
merges tenant and Core actions with Core winning.

Tenant callers read their token's tenant. Core callers select a tenant with `tenantId`; without it only Core
catalogs are returned.

200.description: Catalogs ordered by application; an empty array means none are registered.

get.summary: List events across every namespace in the caller's tenant, newest first.
get.description:
Requires the `audit-reader` role, held in the tenant or as a Core role. Returns only the resolved tenant's
events and accepts the same filters as the namespace listing. Actor `name` and `email` are included as
recorded. Tenant callers read their token's tenant. Core callers must select a tenant with `tenantId`; without it the
request responds 403.

get.summary: Export events across every namespace in the caller's tenant as CSV, newest first.
get.description:
Requires the `audit-reader` role, held in the tenant or as a Core role. Tenant callers read their token's tenant. Core callers must select a tenant with `tenantId`; without it the
request responds 403.

Accepts the same filters as the event listing (`top` and `after` are ignored)
and streams every matching event as CSV, so the export is not capped and is not held in memory.
Cancelling the request stops the export. Actor `name` and `email` columns are present only when the
caller also holds `audit-admin`; for other callers the columns are omitted. Values that a spreadsheet
could read as a formula are prefixed with a single quote. The export is recorded as a `data-access`
audit event with the number of events written.

get.summary: List parked audit events in the resolved tenant.
get.description:
Requires the `audit-admin` role, held in the tenant or as a Core role; `audit-reader` is not enough.
Includes open, replayed and discarded rows, ordered by failed_at descending and id descending.
Tenant callers read their token's tenant and cannot select another tenant. Core administrators must
select a tenant with `tenantId`; without it the request responds 400.

Reads persisted PostgreSQL rows. Paging uses a keyset cursor, so new failures parked while paging do not
shift later pages.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Opaque keyset cursor (failed_at, id) returned as page.next. Stable while new failures are parked.

200.description: Tenant-scoped page. A full page can have a next cursor even if the following page is empty.

after.description: Supplied cursor; omitted on the first page.

post.description:
Requires the `audit-admin` role, held in the tenant or as a Core role. Tenant callers replay in their
token's tenant. Core administrators must select a tenant with `tenantId`; without it the request responds
400. An ID from another tenant responds 404.

No request body is used; the stored input is the source of the original actor and namespace. The Audit
Service is written_by on the recovered audit row, and replayed_as links to that row's id (not its event_id).

PostgreSQL uses a tenant-scoped row lock and one transaction for
the recovered row, status/link update and self-audit in namespace audit-service.
Closed rows return 409, including a second concurrent replay after the first commits.
A failure rolls back all three writes. Replay validates the stored input against the
current action catalog and retention settings, without ingestion's seven-day age limit.

If the same tenant, namespace and event_id already exist, replay links to that row
without changing it. The operation is recorded as failed-event.replay.succeeded.
Startup registers its definition through the SDK into actions-audit-service.
A missing or incompatible registered replay action returns 503 and rolls back the replay.

200.description: Replay transaction committed; the failed row now has status replayed.

400.description: Invalid UUID, invalid or missing tenant context, or a stored event that fails validation; the failed row remains open.

example.errorMessage: Stored event cannot be replayed (unknown_action). Check its action catalog and payload.

404.description: No failed event with this ID in the resolved tenant.

example.errorMessage: failed audit event with ID '3f1c2a9e-7b4d-4e8a-9c21-5d6e7f8a9b0c' could not be found.

409.description: The event has already been replayed or discarded.

example.errorMessage: Only open failed events can be replayed.

get.summary: List the namespaces that have audit events in the caller's tenant.
get.description:
Requires the `audit-reader` role, held in the tenant or as a Core role. Returns every namespace the tenant
has recorded events for, whether or not an action catalog is visible to the tenant (for example core,
platform-level catalogs). Use it to populate a namespace picker. Tenant callers read their token's tenant. Core callers must select a tenant with `tenantId`; without it the
request responds 403.

get.summary: Get the configured retention periods for the caller's tenant.
get.description:
Requires the `audit-reader` role, held in the tenant or as a Core role. Returns the retention periods as the
service applies them at write time: the active configuration revision (falling back to the latest), with Core
settings merged. Only configured periods are returned, not the built-in defaults. Application entries are
included for registered action catalogs that override at least one class. Precedence is built-in defaults,
then `tenant`, then the application entry.

Tenant callers read their token's tenant. Core callers select a tenant with `tenantId`; without it both
properties are empty.

503.description: Retention settings could not be resolved or are out of bounds. Retry.

example.errorMessage: Audit retention settings are temporarily unavailable.

get.description:
Requires the `audit-reader` role, held in the tenant or as a Core role. Returns a JSON array of action
definitions from the caller's tenant merged with Core, with Core winning on duplicate action names.
The namespace is the application identifier in audit-service:actions-<application>.
This endpoint does not require ownership of the namespace.

Tenant callers read their token's tenant. Core callers select a tenant with `tenantId`; without it only the
Core catalog is read.

200.description: Resolved definitions; an empty array means the catalog is registered but empty.

404.description: No action catalog is registered for this namespace (neither Core nor the tenant supplied one). Register the namespace's actions in the audit-service configuration (actions-<application>) and retry. Configuration HTTP or converter failures handled by the SDK can also produce this response.

example.errorMessage: action catalog with ID 'case-service' could not be found.

post.summary: Add an action to the caller's tenant catalog for a namespace.
post.description:
Requires the `audit-admin` role, held in the tenant or as a Core role. The caller's token is forwarded to the
configuration service, so configuration write permission is also required; without it the request responds
401. The action is added to the tenant's actions-<namespace> catalog, which is created if missing.

Tenant callers add to their token's tenant. Core callers must select a tenant with `tenantId`; without it the
request responds 400.

The name is compared in full and case-insensitively with the namespace's own catalog in fresh configuration,
not the cache: 409 when it already exists there or when the namespace is a Core namespace. Names in other
namespaces, including Core ones, are not conflicts.

example.name: case.update
example.description: A case worker updated a case.

201.description: The action was added. The response echoes the added definition.

401.description: Missing or invalid bearer token (plain-text `Unauthorized` body), or the caller lacks permission to change configuration (JSON body).

example.errorMessage: Writing the action catalog requires permission to change configuration.

409.description: The action name exists in the namespace's own catalog, or the namespace is a Core namespace.

example.errorMessage: Action "case.update" already exists in the case-service catalog.

get.summary: List events in a namespace for the caller's tenant, newest first.
get.description:
Requires the `audit-reader` role, held in the tenant or as a Core role. Any reader in the tenant may read any
namespace; ownership is not required for reads. Tenant callers read their token's tenant. Core callers must select a tenant with `tenantId`; without it the
request responds 403.

Filters combine with AND; time bounds are inclusive. Paginate with `top` and `after`. Repeating a query
parameter responds 400.

Responses include `actor.name` and `actor.email` as recorded by the writer, and `audit-reader` callers
receive them. The CSV exports omit name and email unless the caller also holds `audit-admin`.
`retentionUntil` is fixed when the event is written. Successful reads are recorded as audit events in the
`audit-service` namespace.

post.summary: Validate and submit a batch of audit events.
post.description:
**A `202` does not mean every event was stored.** The body reports a per-event outcome:
`accepted`, `duplicates` and `rejected`. Always inspect `rejected`; rejected events are
not stored and are never retried by the service, so the caller must correct and resend them.

**Role:** requires the `audit-writer` role, held in the tenant or as a Core role.

**Namespace ownership:** the verified token's `azp` must be a service URN. A non-Core caller may
write only to the namespace equal to that service's name, and only for its own tenant; any other
namespace returns `403`. Core service accounts with `audit-writer` are exempt from the namespace
check, may select any namespace, and must provide `tenantId`. Grant the writer role only to
authorized service accounts; the platform Core check does not distinguish service accounts from human users.

**Limits:** 1 to 500 events per request; `metadata` and `changeSet` are each limited to 16 KiB.
`eventId` must be a UUID. `occurredAt` must be no more than 7 days in the past and no more than
5 minutes in the future.

**Server-set fields:** `tenantId`, `writtenBy`, `namespace`, `receivedAt`, `category`, `severity`
and `retentionClass` are set by the service from the verified token, the path, the clock and the
registered action. If supplied in an event they are ignored.

Malformed envelopes fail the request; invalid events are rejected individually.
Metadata and changeSet each have a 16 KiB UTF-8 JSON limit, including JSON syntax.
The complete request body is limited to 20 MiB. Server-owned row fields are
always derived from the verified caller, path, clock and resolved action/policy;
additional event fields are not copied into trusted row columns.

Each pod buffers at most 1,000 events and 8 MiB of serialized enriched events,
including retained original input. A batch that cannot fit in an empty buffer
returns 413 without storing any events; split it into smaller requests.
Temporary buffer pressure returns 503 with Retry-After instead.

**Rate limit:** writes are limited per tenant and namespace, counted in events rather
than requests (one request of 500 events uses 500 units). The platform default is
500 events per second with a 500-event burst, per pod. A request over the limit
returns 429 with Retry-After and none of its events are stored. 429 means this
writer is sending too much; 503 means the service cannot keep up with all writers.
Admitted events consume allowance even if storage later fails; retries remain
rate limited during outages. Core defaults and tenant overrides are capped at
500 events per second per tenant and namespace, per pod.

Configuration uses the SDK's existing error handling: HTTP and conversion
failures can resolve to null. Such failures cannot reliably be distinguished
from missing documents and may produce unknown-action rejections, partial
catalogs or fallback retention periods. Only errors that propagate reach
the endpoint's 503 handling.

A 202 waits for the submitter to commit valid events or durably park storage
failures in PostgreSQL. Duplicate eventId values within the same tenant and
namespace do not overwrite existing events. If neither event nor failed-event
storage succeeds, the request returns 503. Requests with only validation
rejections can return 202 without storage.

parameters.name: tenantId
parameters.description: Tenant URN, for example urn:ads:platform:tenant-service:v2:/tenants/case-team. Required for Core writers (400 without it); leave empty as a tenant caller, who cannot select a different tenant.

202.description:
The request was processed, **not** necessarily stored in full. Every input is accepted, a duplicate,
or rejected; accepted + duplicates + rejected.length equals the input count. Check `rejected`:
rejected events are not stored and are not resent. Correct them and submit again.

400.description: Malformed JSON or envelope (for example no events or more than 500), invalid namespace or tenant ID, or missing Core tenant context. Fix the request; do not retry unchanged.

example.errorMessage: Validation failed with error(s): events (body) - events must be an array containing 1 to 500 events.

403.description:
Either the caller lacks the `audit-writer` role (have it granted to the service account), or the
namespace is not the caller's: a non-Core caller can write only to its own service's namespace and
tenant. A token whose `azp` is not a service URN is also refused.

example.errorMessage: User Case service (ID: 5c1d2e3f-4a5b-4c6d-8e7f-9a0b1c2d3e4f) not permitted to write audit events in another namespace.

413.description: Request body exceeds 20 MiB, or the enriched batch exceeds the 8 MiB buffer capacity. Split the batch; retrying it unchanged will not help.

example.errorMessage: Audit request exceeds the 20 MB body limit.

429.description: The tenant and namespace exceeded the write rate limit. No events in the request were stored; resend the whole request after Retry-After.

Retry-After.description: Seconds until enough allowance has accumulated for this request, assuming no competing writes for the same tenant and namespace.

example.errorMessage: Audit write rate limit exceeded for this tenant and namespace. Retry after the Retry-After delay.

503.description: Configuration, retention policy or durable storage is unavailable, or the buffer is temporarily full; retry without re-registering actions.

Retry-After.description: Minimum suggested retry delay in seconds.

get.summary: Export one namespace's events as CSV, newest first.
get.description:
Requires the `audit-reader` role, held in the tenant or as a Core role. Behaves as the export across all
namespaces, limited to the namespace. Tenant callers read their token's tenant. Core callers must select a tenant with `tenantId`; without it the
request responds 403.

get.summary: Read one event by its service-generated id.
get.description:
Requires the `audit-reader` role, held in the tenant or as a Core role. Use the service-generated `id` of a
listed event, not the writer's `eventId`. An id belonging to another tenant returns 404. Actor `name` and
`email` are included as recorded. Tenant callers read their token's tenant. Core callers must select a tenant with `tenantId`; without it the
request responds 403.

404.description: Event not found in the caller's tenant and namespace. IDs from another tenant also respond 404.

example.errorMessage: audit event with ID '9a8b7c6d-5e4f-4a3b-8c2d-1e0f9a8b7c6d' could not be found.

After.name: after
After.description: Opaque keyset cursor from page.next of the previous response. Stable while new events arrive. An invalid cursor returns 400.

AuditNamespace.name: namespace
AuditNamespace.description: Audit namespace, the application name of the writing service (for example `case-service`).

FailedEventsTenant.name: tenantId
FailedEventsTenant.description: Tenant URN, for example urn:ads:platform:tenant-service:v2:/tenants/case-team. Required for Core administrators; leave empty as a tenant caller, who cannot select another tenant.

OccurredFrom.name: occurredFrom
OccurredFrom.description: Inclusive lower bound, as an ISO 8601 date or date-time.

OccurredTo.name: occurredTo
OccurredTo.description: Inclusive upper bound. Must not be before occurredFrom.

Scope.name: scope
Scope.description: Matches events whose scopeIds contain this value.

TenantId.name: tenantId
TenantId.description: Tenant URN, for example urn:ads:platform:tenant-service:v2:/tenants/case-team. Selects the tenant for Core callers. Leave empty as a tenant caller, who always acts on the token's tenant; supplying any other tenant returns 403. A value that is not a tenant URN returns 400.

AuditBadRequest.description: The request is invalid: a path or query parameter failed validation, `tenantId` is not a tenant URN, or a required tenant context is missing. Fix the request; do not retry unchanged.

example.errorMessage: Validation failed with error(s): namespace (params) - Invalid value

AuditCatalogUnavailable.description: Action catalogs could not be read or checked. Retry; do not re-register actions.

example.errorMessage: Action catalog is temporarily unavailable. Retry the request; do not re-register actions.

AuditEventCsv.description: The matching events as CSV, with one header row.

AuditEventPage.description: A page of events, newest first by occurredAt.

next.description: Present when more results may exist.

AuditForbidden.description: The caller lacks the role the operation requires, or a tenant caller set `tenantId` to another tenant. Have the role granted to the caller; provisioning a role in the realm does not assign it.

example.errorMessage: User Case reader (ID: 4f9e2d1c-8a7b-4c6d-9e5f-1a2b3c4d5e6f) not permitted to access audit data requiring audit-reader.

AuditStorageUnavailable.description: Audit event storage is unavailable. Retry.

example.errorMessage: Audit event storage is unavailable. Retry the request.

AuditUnauthorized.description: Missing or invalid bearer token. Obtain a valid token and retry.

FailedEventsUnavailable.description: Database, action configuration or transactional self-auditing is unavailable; retry.

name.description: Base action name, without a terminal `.succeeded` or `.failed` suffix.

retentionClass.description: Named retention class; custom classes are allowed. Never a duration. Optional: when omitted, the class is derived from the category (administrative and data-access: compliance, security: security, runtime and diagnostic: standard). A class set on the action overrides the category default.

metadataSchema.description: Optional JSON Schema draft-07 for metadata; omitted means no action-specific metadata constraint.

example.name: case.update
example.description: A case worker updated a case.

core.description: True when Core registers a catalog for the application, so its actions are not tenant-managed.

example.errorMessage: Validation failed with error(s): top (query) - Invalid value

AuditEvent.description: A stored event. tenant_id is never returned.

AuditEventInput.description: One event to write. Server-set fields (tenantId, writtenBy, namespace, receivedAt, category, severity, retentionClass) are ignored if supplied.

eventId.description: Caller UUID; database uniqueness is scoped to tenant and namespace.

occurredAt.description: No more than 7 days old or 5 minutes in the future, inclusive.

action.description: Registered base action with an optional terminal .succeeded or .failed suffix.

actionVersion.description: Omitted means the current catalog version; an explicit mismatch is rejected individually.

resource.description: Required if the action declares resourceType; type must match.

metadata.description: At most 16 KiB serialized UTF-8 JSON. Validated against metadataSchema without coercion or adding defaults.

changeSet.description:
At most 16 KiB serialized UTF-8 JSON. Shape is validated only when the
action captures change sets; otherwise the value is dropped from row
columns rather than rejected for its shape. The byte limit still applies.

index.description: Zero-based index in the original request; results are sorted by index. Use it, and eventId when present, to identify which event the entry concerns.

event.description: Original stored JSON input. Only audit-admin may access this potentially sensitive payload.

tags.name: Audit events
tags.description: Write and read audit events. Requires audit-writer to write and audit-reader to read.

tags.name: Action catalogs
tags.description: Read the registered action definitions for a namespace. Requires audit-reader.

tags.name: Failed audit events
tags.description: List and replay events parked after a storage failure. Requires audit-admin.

tags.name: Retention
tags.description: Read the configured retention periods for a tenant. Requires audit-reader.
